title: Moderated usability vignettes and wireframe reactions — May 2025
content:
Purpose:
Run 6 moderated sessions (45m each) to validate next-iteration wireframes for the Console's route-level settings, rollout controls, and a compact model-selection flow. Quick capture for engineering + design to use in grooming session on 2025-05-22.

Participants (recruit):
- U1: Platform engineer at mid-market SaaS (has on-call, manages dedicated capacity)
- U2: ML engineer at startup (uses hosted API + occasional dedicated clusters)
- U3: Solutions engineer from partner (demo-heavy)
- U4: Product manager for search product (embedding + rerank consumer)
- U5: Internal SRE (console power-user)
- U6: Beta customer (enterprise security, uses Private deployment)

Test tasks (short vignettes):
1) Update route to pin model v2.3 for traffic A, enable canary of v2.4 at 10% and set fallback to v2.2.
2) Diagnose why a recent request shows elevated latency for route /chat/structured and find the top suspect cause.
3) Create an autoscaling policy that allows bursts for traffic spikes but keeps baseline reserved GPUs for SLA.
4) Interpret the cost breakdown (token + compute) for a single logged request and explain to a teammate.
5) Use the lightweight ‘quick-run’ (dev-mode) to test a prompt and save it as an evaluation case.

High-level findings (top 5):
- Mental model mismatch: "Pinning" vs "versioning" confused several participants. They expected pin to be scoped locally (dev environment) but pinning currently applies globally to the route. Quote: "I thought pinning meant stick this to my session, not the whole prod route" (U2).
- Canary feedback visibility weak: participants could create a canary but weren't confident how to read rollout application across regions and tiers. They look for a live map or quick summary that shows % by region.
- Cost transparency: the per-request cost card is useful, but token counts and GPU-cost split felt abstract. U4 asked for a comparative baseline (how this request compares to 95th percentile).
- Quick-run vs full-run signals: the dev quick-run button lacks explicit SLO/latency expectations. Several users expected it to route to dedicated test pool — they were surprised when it hit production pool and saw real quotas consumed.
- Failure mode visibility: fallback policy is not discoverable when a model variant is incompatible (different tokenizer, e.g.). One SRE said: "Why did traffic drop to fallback without a clear reason? Where's the error?" (U5).

Wireframe-specific reactions (items that map to tickets):
- Model selection control (compact dropdown): users liked the compact layout but wanted a clarification tooltip and a small icon that indicates "quantized / fp16 / pruned". Suggestion: include a micro-label under model name (e.g., gptx-16q) and hover details. -> Backlog: P1, owner: eng-runtime (JIRA: PI-78).
- Rollout slider: several participants tried clicking the percent label to type; they expected direct input. Wireframe only had drag handle. Quick fix: add editable percent input box and keyboard arrows. -> Backlog: P2, owner: product-console (JIRA: CON-4523).
- Canary region summary: want a condensed badge next to rollout showing region breakdown. Mockup idea: small chevron to expand region rows; default collapsed. -> Backlog: P2, owner: product + infra.
- Cost breakdown card: add a baseline comparison (95th percentile) and a tooltip that translates compute minutes to $ cents. Also include a link to optimize suggestions when cost > threshold. -> Backlog: P3, owner: product-optimize.
- Dev-run isolation indicator: add a persistent yellow pill when quick-run is isolated (dev pool) or red if it will consume prod capacity. Make dev-run default to isolated in demo builds. -> Backlog: P1, owner: release-engineering.

Micro-observations (fast hits):
- Small text contrast issue on the latency badge (low contrast on 13px).
- Users expected copy on hover for the KV cache toggle: what does turning it off mean for latency?
- A11y: rollout slider not reachable by keyboard in current prototype.
- Users using touch laptops tried to tap-and-hold the timeline to scrub; consider adding touch affordances.

Representative quotes (verbatim):
- U1: "I don't want to be the person who pins the wrong thing — can we show a confirmation that lists affected environments?"
- U3: "This cost thing is forensic; give me a quick signal: green/yellow/red with suggested action."
- U6: "Audit trail for who changed rollout is non-negotiable for us. Where's the link to the audit log?"

Backlog grooming notes (for 05-22 grooming):
- Consolidate model-info micro-labels into a single component (design + tokens): 2 d for design, 3 d for eng. Scope: label + hover panel. Priority: P1.
- Add editable percent input & keyboard support to rollout slider: 1 d design, 2 d frontend. Priority: P2.
- Canary region badge + expand/collapse rows: research scope (1 d), build (3 d infra + api). Priority: P2.
- Cost baseline + quick-optimize link: design 1 d, implement 2 d + backend metric exposure. Priority: P3.
- Quick-run isolation default for sandbox builds: coordinate with release eng, small config change. Priority: P1.

Open questions / assumptions to validate:
- Assumption: most users treat "pin" as a persistent route-level action. We need analytics check (last 6 months) on pin usage to confirm. (Action: data-req to analytics).
- Question: Should audit log links appear inline next to every rollout change or only in detailed change view? (Product decision)
- Assumption: A small percentage (>10%) of requests in dev quick-run currently hit prod pool due to misconfigured routing in staging. Need infra confirmation. (Action: SRE follow-up with release-engineering).

Session artifacts & where recordings live:
- Recordings: drive link (internal) -> CON-4521/recordings (see linked artifacts).
- Raw transcripts: attached to ticket JIRA-PI-78 (internal).

Next steps (short-term, before grooming meeting):
- Aisha: pull analytics on pin usage & quick-run routing (due 2025-05-18).
- Jon: create skeleton PR for rollout input + keyboard support (due 2025-05-19).
- Design: Lena to produce micro-label comps and tooltip copy (due 2025-05-19).
- Ops: Maya to confirm dev pool isolation config and share rollback plan if default toggles change (due 2025-05-18).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep wireframes lean — users prefer concise summaries + one-click deep dive. Avoid full-page tables for simple actions.
- Bring customer-security to the convo for audit-log expectations (U6 strong requirement).
- We should schedule a brief follow-up with U2 to validate new micro-label language (they were very sensitive to naming).

Appendix (quick sketches):
- Sketch A: compact model row with micro-label + small info chevron
- Sketch B: rollout slider with inline percent input and region badge
- Sketch C: request card with 95th percentile baseline chip and small optimize CTA

End notes: overall signal positive — participants liked the compact approach and the intent behind the changes. Biggest immediate risk: miscommunication about "pin" semantics and quick-run routing. Focus grooming on those two items first.
